scope: Software supply-chain controls and Solana client/indexing compatibility
method: Pinned official repository README and license/source inspection with upstream HEAD revisions recorded. Findings are bounded research notes; no REA execution, packages installed, SYLPH code patch, build, or runtime test was performed.

provenance: Official Semgrep README and repository license metadata inspected at pinned develop commit 51602ad27f09ef9342a5620601de5ef8f572fbc6; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: Semgrep is a pattern-based static analysis tool that supports many languages and can run locally, in pre-commit, or CI.
The README warns that Community Edition has single-function/file scope and can miss security findings requiring cross-file or cross-function analysis.
The repository is LGPL-2.1; commercial platform features and rules are distinct from the open-source engine and need separate scope review.
patterns: Add local static checks for risky source patterns around authorization, secret logging, unchecked parsing, and unsafe state transitions.
Treat clean scans as incomplete evidence; combine with tests, code review, and dependency/security analysis.
overlap: Adds static-analysis coverage but does not replace TypeScript compiler, tests, or independent safety review.
risks: Community Edition has documented analysis limitations and may miss interprocedural issues.
False positives require triage; findings do not establish exploitability.
LGPL and paid platform/rule scope require license review before adoption.
validation: Run locally/CI without credentials; define reviewed rules and test each against positive and negative snippets.
Track known coverage boundaries and require existing deterministic regression suites for critical behavior.
sources.license: LGPL-2.1 (repository metadata; platform/rule licensing may differ)

provenance: Official StrykerJS README and Apache license metadata inspected at pinned master commit c931a93237816901f1e9f48da411170beeb3dfca; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: StrykerJS performs mutation testing for JavaScript/TypeScript by altering production code and checking whether the test suite detects those changes.
Mutation score is a measure of test sensitivity to generated mutations, not correctness or safety certification.
The repository declares Apache-2.0 licensing.
patterns: Use targeted mutation testing on high-value pure functions and gates to find tests that pass even when a guard or comparison is removed.
Record surviving mutants and review whether they expose a test gap or an intentional equivalent mutation.
overlap: Complements deterministic tests; no runtime integration.
risks: Full-suite mutation runs can be expensive and noisy.
Mutation tools can miss semantic faults outside the mutation operators.
A high score must not be represented as proof of financial safety.
validation: Pilot against isolated pure functions and thresholds; verify known mutants are killed and equivalent mutants are documented.
Do not run against live processes or alter production artifacts.

provenance: Official Renovate README and license metadata inspected at pinned main commit 20767551404255f954569588dc1db726dfe791d6; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: Renovate is a dependency-update automation CLI that can propose version changes across multiple package managers.
Its repository is AGPL-3.0; configuration and self-hosted/service use should be reviewed against license requirements.
Automated update PRs still need lockfile, build, tests, and vulnerability review; version automation itself is not compatibility evidence.
patterns: Use scheduled, grouped dependency update proposals with explicit package allowlists, version constraints, and CI verification.
Separate direct dependency changes from transitive lockfile churn to make review and rollback easier.
overlap: Can complement existing dependency maintenance; no runtime module should call Renovate.
risks: AGPL-3.0 terms apply to the tool; hosted service terms may differ.
Broad automation can introduce breaking or compromised updates if reviews/checks are bypassed.
Automated merge is inappropriate for dependencies that affect signing, execution, or safety boundaries.
validation: Test in a draft configuration against a non-production branch; require CI and human review for all updates.
Pin update workflow permissions to least privilege and avoid auto-merge on safety-critical dependencies.

provenance: Official Cosign README and Apache license metadata inspected at pinned main commit 63d9aa14a70c03e73c7b2a2a9a6501566194f5f4; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: Cosign signs and verifies container images and other artifacts, including keyless signing with Fulcio certificates and Rekor transparency log integration.
The README also lists hardware/KMS and key-pair signing methods; keyless artifact verification does not grant or use SYLPH wallet authority.
The repository declares Apache-2.0 licensing.
patterns: Verify release artifacts against pinned publisher identity and expected source before packaging or deployment.
Record artifact digest, signature identity, certificate, transparency evidence, and verifier version in release attestations.
overlap: Supply-chain artifact assurance can complement existing release certification; it does not certify runtime state or a trade.
risks: Signing identity policy and trust roots must be configured correctly; a valid signature alone does not prove a safe artifact.
Keyless verification depends on certificate identity and transparency evidence validation.
Do not conflate software artifact signing with wallet transaction signing.
validation: Verify known-good and tampered test artifacts with pinned identity constraints and expected transparency evidence.
Keep signing keys and credentials outside source control and avoid introducing wallet/key access.

provenance: Official Rekor README and Apache license metadata inspected at pinned main commit 774b191f9f761b3def5808bcd54b48ad88de5f89; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: Rekor is a software-supply-chain transparency log intended to record and search signed artifact metadata.
Cosign documents Rekor as part of its keyless-signing flow; Rekor entries add public provenance evidence but do not independently establish publisher trust.
The repository declares Apache-2.0 licensing.
patterns: Store verifiable build/release attestations for shipped SYLPH artifacts and bind them to immutable content digests.
Verify inclusion/proof and expected signer identity rather than relying on a log lookup or URL alone.
overlap: Pairs with Cosign and overlaps with other catalog supply-chain tools; no application runtime integration required.
risks: Transparency log inclusion does not itself guarantee the artifact is benign or source-complete.
Verifier trust policy and identity allowlists must be explicit.
External log/network availability should not affect Engine runtime or trading readiness.
validation: Test inclusion proof verification, digest mismatch rejection, wrong signer identity, and unavailable-log/offline behavior in release CI.
Preserve verification output with the artifact manifest and pinned verifier version.

provenance: Official Trivy README and license metadata inspected at pinned main commit 088b9706d7e3af33ef1a8d2dee305370df714293; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: Trivy scans filesystems, remote Git repositories, images, VMs and Kubernetes for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, secrets, SBOM and license data.
Its scanners cover OS and language dependencies; results depend on target, selected scanners and vulnerability database state.
The repository documents Apache-2.0 licensing and warns that per-main-push canary builds may contain critical bugs and are not recommended for production.
patterns: Scan the pinned source tree, lockfiles and any release image in CI using a pinned stable scanner and recorded database metadata.
Retain machine-readable findings and triage them with code review; a clean scan is not proof of security or exploitability.
overlap: Complements source review and dependency audits; no runtime role.
risks: Database freshness and scanner coverage affect findings.
Canary builds are explicitly not recommended for production.
Scanner findings require triage and do not prove exploitability.
validation: Use a pinned stable version against known vulnerable and clean fixtures.
Record database metadata and review ignored paths, severities and image/source scope.

provenance: Official OSV-Scanner README and license metadata inspected at pinned main commit f455353546889009663c1f8b640d5880a01c889a; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: OSV-Scanner maps supported dependency manifests and package ecosystems to vulnerability records in the OSV database.
Its README documents package-manager and container scanning plus guided dependency remediation; results inform maintenance but do not make upgrades safe automatically.
The repository declares Apache-2.0 licensing and uses OSV-Scalibr for package and project-type analysis.
patterns: Include a pinned scanner invocation in CI and archive machine-readable findings plus database/version context.
Review direct and transitive advisories and run regression/build checks before applying any suggested dependency upgrade.
overlap: Supply-chain review only; does not affect runtime decisions.
risks: Advisory matching and package/version data may be incomplete or ambiguous.
Suggested upgrades can change behavior and must be tested before merge.
Scanner or database versions can change results.
validation: Test against known vulnerable and clean lockfile fixtures.
Record scanner version, advisory data timestamp and accepted exceptions.

provenance: Official Gitleaks README and MIT license metadata inspected at pinned master commit b58d3f102cf3a2c84cb7f923d05c25c9b1aed84b; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: Gitleaks scans files, Git history and stdin for credential-like secrets, with pre-commit and CI integration documented.
The README marks the project feature-complete and says future releases are security patches only, directing new feature work toward Betterleaks.
Its rules, baselines and allowlists affect coverage; scan reports may contain sensitive matched material and require restricted handling.
patterns: Run a pinned secret scan on diffs and repository history with reports kept access-controlled and redacted before sharing.
Treat any suspected real match as a secret-handling incident; the scanner cannot revoke or rotate credentials.
overlap: Potential CI tool only; no credential or signer integration.
risks: False positives and allowlists can hide real secrets.
Reports may expose matching secret values.
Project is feature-complete with security-patch-only future releases.
validation: Use fabricated dummy secrets and expected nonmatches in isolated fixtures.
Review allowlist edits and protect generated reports.

provenance: Official OPA README and Apache license metadata inspected at pinned main commit 89d111ce4b45c3af9b79ac1137efe2e9aab6cc92; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: OPA is a general-purpose policy engine; policy authors express context-aware decisions in Rego against caller-supplied input.
OPA provides local CLI and integration/deployment paths; application code remains responsible for consuming and enforcing decisions.
The repository declares Apache-2.0 licensing; this review does not establish an external policy service as suitable for SYLPH capital or signing authority.
patterns: Use policy-as-code for offline release/deployment checks with explicit input schemas and fail-closed handling.
Keep the trusted in-process execution authority as the enforcement boundary; policy output can only add a restriction, never grant bypass authority.
overlap: Could model static release predicates, but no OPA process or policy is added to the runtime.
risks: Incomplete input or a mistaken default can yield an unsafe allow.
Service outages or policy bundle drift must not bypass trusted local restrictions.
Policy checks do not replace authorization and capital controls.
validation: Test allow/deny, missing-field, malformed-input and timeout cases.
Prove policy failure cannot skip existing execution authority.

provenance: Official CodeQL query/library README and repository license inspected at pinned main commit dd4405c2c2a8cd5ee7d200e7230ab8dd52e13dc6; accessed 2026-10-15.
discoveries: The repository contains standard CodeQL libraries and queries used by GitHub code scanning and application-security products.
The query/library repository is MIT-licensed, while the CodeQL CLI and analysis engine are in another repository and separately licensed.
The README states that use of the CodeQL CLI to analyze closed-source code requires a separate commercial license.
patterns: Use supported code scanning for source-level security queries only after confirming licensing and language support.
Add custom queries only with reviewed positive/negative test fixtures and treat findings as signals for human review.
overlap: Static analysis can complement tests and reviews; the query repo alone does not supply an unrestricted scanner license.
risks: CLI/engine licensing differs from the MIT query/library repository.
Findings need triage and do not prove the absence of vulnerabilities.
Language and query coverage may not include every relevant TypeScript behavior.
validation: Verify code-scanning entitlement for the repository and intended use.
Test custom query matches and nonmatches on minimal fixtures; preserve tool version and results.
sources.license: MIT (query/library repository); CodeQL CLI/engine separately licensed, including closed-source analysis entitlement

provenance: Official Solana Program Library Token-2022 repository and docs; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Token-2022 program supports extensions that alter token-account or mint behavior.
Integrators need to inspect enabled extensions rather than assume legacy SPL Token semantics.
The canonical TransferFee.calculate_fee uses ceiling division for fractional raw units, then caps the result at maximum_fee; floor-based calculations understate some fees.
patterns: Parse token program ID and extension state before modeling transfer semantics.
Use checked arithmetic and explicit transfer-fee accounting where applicable.
Mirror the canonical ceil-rounding and maximum-fee cap with raw-unit boundary fixtures.
overlap: Extends existing token compatibility; no broad integration without extension-specific needs.
risks: Unsupported extensions can invalidate quote, transfer or net-PnL assumptions.
Program upgrades and SDK versions require pinning.
validation: Build fixtures for supported/unsupported extension combinations.
Compare quote, simulation and confirmed transfer amounts.
Test fractional one-unit fees, maximum-fee caps, zero and 10000 bps against pinned Token-2022 semantics.

provenance: Official Blockdaemon AccountsDB Kafka plugin repository; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Validator AccountsDB plugin exports account updates to Kafka.
It is infrastructure-side account streaming, distinct from ordinary client RPC polling.
patterns: Preserve slot, write version and account identity in streamed records.
Use consumer checkpoints and gap reconciliation for restart recovery.
overlap: Alternative upstream data transport; overlaps at the account-event ingestion boundary.
risks: Requires validator/plugin access and Kafka operations.
Account update delivery alone may not supply full transaction semantics.
validation: Test ordering, duplicate, disconnect and restart behavior on isolated fixtures.
Reconcile sampled account state against canonical RPC reads.
sources.license: Not independently verified in this review

provenance: Official Solana Foundation solana-web3.js repository; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Current repository describes a v3+ pnpm workspace, while legacy v1.x is on a maintenance branch with critical fixes only.
Packages are independently versioned; root workspace is orchestration rather than the published client package.
patterns: Pin exact client major/version and test RPC serialization behavior.
Treat migration between v1 and v3 as an explicit compatibility project.
overlap: Client SDK choice must align with existing interfaces; avoid duplicate Solana client abstraction without a concrete migration need.
risks: Major version behavior and types may differ.
Incompatible transaction serialization can break signing/fee accounting.
validation: Test transaction/message serialization, RPC errors and versioned transaction fixtures.
Keep signer/custody restrictions unchanged during any upgrade.

provenance: Official Meteora DBC SDK repository and developer guide; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: SDK targets Meteora Dynamic Bonding Curve launch pools, quoting/trading helpers and migration lifecycle.
Official developer guide describes migration of completed DBC pools to DAMM v2 and separate program/account flows.
patterns: Model launch state and graduation destination explicitly per mint/pool.
Keep quote math and lifecycle transitions versioned by program/SDK revision.
overlap: Adds venue-specific lifecycle coverage to existing AMM bridge; avoid generic assumptions that every token graduates to one venue.
risks: Program IDs, account layouts, fees and migration behavior can change.
Transfer hooks/extensions may affect executable quotes.
validation: Use official fixtures/program IDs and test lifecycle transitions on local/test environments.
Compare SDK quote results with on-chain simulation and confirmed amounts.
sources.license: Not independently verified in this review

provenance: Official Carbon repository and documentation; accessed 2026-10-14.
discoveries: Carbon is an indexing framework for decoding Solana transactions/accounts into data pipelines.
Decoders and datasource transports are composable, so versioned program decoders can be isolated.
patterns: Use independently tested decoders per program and retain raw event provenance.
Separate ingestion transport from protocol-specific decoding.
overlap: Conceptually overlaps the current canonical ingress and decoders; adopt patterns, not a parallel ingestion engine.
risks: Decoder coverage may lag protocol changes.
Third-party index outputs are not canonical state without reconciliation.
validation: Test decoders with captured versioned transactions and malformed inputs.
Compare decoded events to RPC/account state and source receipts.
